name: CO-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district (D+11 PVI) with incumbent Jason Crow running
Crow's $3.2M raised and $2.7M cash on hand versus a minimally funded challenger
Prediction markets price Crow at ~96% to win
model.rationale: The baseline of D+21.6 rests on a solid partisan lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge, with no polls or ratings suggesting any reason to move. Polymarket's 96% for Crow corroborates a Safe D rating, so I hold near the baseline with slightly tightened uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Crow under 55% or significant outside spending against him would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Crow, the Democratic incumbent in Colorado's 6th District, is seeking another term in a seat that leans about eleven points Democratic. He has raised over $3.1 million and holds $2.7 million on hand, while his Republican challenger, Jason Clark, reports no fundraising figures. Minor-party and independent candidates trail far behind, with one independent carrying negative cash on hand.

With no public polling, no expert ratings, and no relevant headlines, the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, both of which point the same way. Polymarket prices Crow at roughly 96 percent, consistent with a Safe D call near a twenty-point expected margin.
